41.0.0.en: 1 "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or press down his tongue with a cord? 2 Canst thou put a rope into his snout? or bore his jaw through with a hook? 3 Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee? 4 Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever? 5 Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens? 6 Shall the company of fishers dig a pit for him? or shall they part him among the Canaanites? 7 Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears? 8 Lay thine hand upon him; remember the battle no more! 9 Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? 10 None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

41.0.1.en: Canst thou draw out the crocodile with an hook, or press down his tongue with a cord? [1]

41.0.2.en: In God's discourse with Job about Satan, He wants to assure him that, with all his power and violence, he is, for the believer, nothing but something like a fish that can be caught with a small fishing rod.

41.0.3.en: Leviathan, by which Satan is meant here. Opinions about this name are many, of which we mention: 1. A huge water animal, violent and predatory. The Septuagint has Dralaonate, that is, dragon, as also in the Syriac and the old Arabic. The false prophet and the antichrist have been likened to the sea dragon and the land dragon [Rev 13]. 2. A deadly and unique kind of poisonous serpent. Some Jewish stories mention a huge serpent that coils around the whole earth, spewing its poisons. 3. A kind of deadly whale. 4. The crocodile of the river Nile is meant, as Bochart said. 5. Hasaeus holds that it is not a whale but the Orca, a water monster (a fearsome animal of strange shape), armed with sharp teeth, which terrifies the whales. 6. Grotius holds that it is a very huge fish called the mular or musar, found in the Mediterranean Sea. 7. Some, such as Schultens, hold that it is a symbolic name representing ancient terrifying animals, by which Satan is meant. 8. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that his name may be called Leviathan as a kind of irony, since the word means something huge and dreadful.

41.0.4.en: Those who say that it is the crocodile rely on the following: 1. There are no whales in the Mediterranean or in the rivers of that region, but the crocodile is found in the river Nile and some rivers of Asia and Africa, so most likely Job had no knowledge of whales but of crocodiles. It is true that the Speaker is God and He knows all that He created, but He does not speak to Job of an animal that he had not heard of or known. 2. The characteristics given here of Leviathan apply to the crocodile, in that it is savage, violent and cannot be controlled. Its mouth is fearful and its size very great, armed with a huge row of teeth and covered with scales close together, and it is distinguished by its terrible eyes. It cannot be caught by the ordinary means of catching beasts of prey. (Its length is usually between 18 and 20 feet, but it sometimes reaches thirty feet.) The number of its very sharp teeth is 30 or more in each jaw. It is considered one of the most fearsome water animals. It often swims on the surface of the water to catch any animal it finds, and if it finds no food it approaches the bank and hides among the papyrus leaves, so that when any animal comes near to drink it pounces on it and drags it into the water to drown and eat it. It is famous for catching tigers that come to drink. 3. What supports the supposition that it is the crocodile is what is mentioned in Job 40:15 about behemoth, which is an animal of the water. Perhaps the two lived in the same region, for if behemoth is the sea horse or the behemoth or the sea giant, the hippopotamus, which was in the river Nile, then Leviathan is the crocodile found in the same river. Some drawings in Herculaneum show Egyptian landscapes in which we see the crocodile lying among the (water) reeds and the sea horse on the plants on an island. Also the famous mosaic in Praeneste represents the plants and animals of Egypt and Ethiopia. The sea horse and the crocodile are indicated together in one group on the Nile. Herodotus indicates that some Egyptians consider the crocodile sacred, while others attack it. Sometimes they treat it with excessive honor and offer it fish and precious foods, and adorn its head with earrings and its feet with bracelets and gold rings inlaid with precious stones. They tame it very gently, and after its death they embalm it with precious spices; this in regions such as Thebes and Owbite and Arsinoite and Maabdeh, opposite the present city of Manfalut. And in other regions they treated it with great disgust, and let no opportunity pass in which they could destroy it.

41.0.5.en: Gesenws holds that Leviathan is derived from Laowah (to twist), where one creature bends around another and coils around it, perhaps to destroy or devour it.

41.0.6.en: Herodotus mentions that among the ways of catching the crocodile, they put a piece of pork on a hook (a fishing rod) and throw it on the water to float, and then bring a live pig to the bank and beat it until it screams. The crocodile comes to the bank at the sound of its screaming to seize it, and when it finds the piece of meat it swallows it, and they pull it with the rod toward the bank, and the first thing they do to it is fill its eyes with mud so that they can control it.

41.0.7.en: The crocodile has no tongue, or has a very small tongue attached to the lower jaw; but just as in fishing the fish draws the hook with the bait through its tongue, so God asks whether Leviathan can be drawn by his tongue.

41.0.8.en: Thevenot holds that some used to dig pits on the bank and cover them with sticks, and when the crocodile falls into one of them it cannot get out. They leave it for several days without food, and then bind its jaw with ropes which they knot around it, and then drag it.

41.0.9.en: God directs our eyes to the enemy of all mankind: if it is hard to catch Leviathan with a hook and drag him out by his tongue with a cord, what will they do with the devil?

41.0.10.en: The devil is exceedingly violent and hard to overcome, but the Son of the living God came down to our earth, and when He became incarnate, this body of His, or His humanity, became the hook with which He catches him. The devil thought regarding Christ that, since He bore a body like all the children of men, and had a human soul, he had authority over Him, and could take Him into his kingdom of darkness. He stirred up his followers to crucify Him, reckoning this a victory over Him, and he did not realize the hook set for him, for by the Cross He put him to shame, deprived him of his authority, and drew out from him the captives who had fallen under his authority.

41.0.11.en: The Lord left the enemy of good and his followers to blaspheme Him and bring accusations against Him, and the enemy did not realize that by this he was being drawn by his tongue to go down to Gehenna, he and his angels who shared his blasphemy against the Savior of the world.

41.0.12.en: * Leviathan was caught with a fishing hook, when he was seized by the bait of the body of our Savior, for by the sharp prick of His divinity it pierced him at once. The hook caught him as in the throat of one who swallows it, when the bait of the body appeared to the devourer so that he might seize it at the time of His sufferings, and the divinity laid hold of him to kill him.

41.0.13.en: * Understand, O Job, what I do: when I send My only-begotten Son in the flesh to the death of the corrupter, in My Son the mortal body appears, while the power of His immortality does not appear. This is a kind of hook that destroys him who swallows it, by the hiding, with skill, of the power with which it wounds him.

41.0.14.en: "Or press down his tongue with a cord"... For sins are symbolized by the cord, as the prophet says: "Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity" (Isa 5:18)... Also the "cord" expresses faith, as Solomon testifies, saying, "A threefold cord is not quickly broken" (Eccl 4:12). For the faith in the truth, which the mouth of those who preach the knowledge of the Trinity weaves, remains firm in the elect. It is broken only in the heart of the wicked. Here you may understand the word cord as faith or as sin. For our incarnate Lord bound the mouth of Leviathan with a cord, when He appeared in the likeness of sinful flesh and condemned all his sinful teachings... Through the likeness of sinful flesh the deceitful dialogue in the flesh was cooled, the tongue of Leviathan was bound, and when the truth was known, the false teachings fell silent.

41.0.16.en: * Now, my beloved, Satan has been slain, that tyrant who is against the whole world... Death no longer reigns, but life rules instead of death, for the Lord says: "I am... the life" (Jn 14:6), so that everything is filled with joy and gladness, as it is written: [The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice] (a)... Now that death has been abolished and the kingdom of Satan has been destroyed, everything is filled with joy and gladness.

41.0.17.en: * If Satan, the enemy of our race, fell from heaven and turned to our lower realm, he has come to have authority over the spirits of his fellows, whom he uses as his followers, working by deceptions for the sake of disobedience. They work not only in those who are deceived, but they try to hinder those who rise upward, as the Apostle says: "According to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience" (Eph 2:2). The Lord came to drive Satan out and cleanse the air of him, preparing the way to heaven "through the veil, that is to say, his flesh" (Heb 10:20). As the Apostle says: What kind of death can accomplish this except the death that takes place in the air, I mean on the Cross...! It was very fitting for the Lord to endure this death, for by His being lifted up (on the Cross) He cleansed the air of the evil of the devil and of all kinds of demons, for He says: "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Lk 10:18); by this He made a new opening of the way to heaven, for He says also: [Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors] [(Ps 24:7) Septuagint]. For the Word had no need of the opening of the gates, since He is the Lord of all, and none of His works is shut before Him; rather we are the ones who need the gates opened, since He bore us in His body. He offered death on our behalf, paving the way for us to the heavens.

41.0.18.en: * For the Lord touched every part of creation and freed it and set it free from all deceptions of falsehood and illusion, as St. Paul says, when He Himself spoiled principalities and powers, triumphing over them on the Cross. So that no one after Him should be deceived, but should find everywhere the Word of the true God.

41.0.19.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic * The Lord stood firm against the trials that came from the enemy in order to restore the victory to mankind. By this He made Satan a plaything, as David proclaimed: [That leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein] (Ps 104:26)... and also: [Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces upon the waters] (Ps 73:13-14). The Lord declares in the Book of Job that this leviathan becomes a plaything and is caught in this trial: "Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook?" (Job 41:1).

41.0.20.en: Abba Chromatius * Satan is deceived when he wounds himself with his own sting, and he fortifies against himself the one whom he thinks he is weakening. For the holy Job was fortified all the more when he wounded him, he who covered his whole body with sores, and he bore the stings of Satan and his poison did not affect him. Therefore it was well said to him: "Thou shalt draw out the dragon with a hook, and play with him as with a bird. Thou shalt bind him as a child does a sparrow, and lay thy hand upon him" (Job 41:1, 5, 8) LXX.

41.0.21.en: You see how Paul mocked him, as a child, as it is in the prophecy, put his hand on the hole of the serpent, and the snake did not hurt him. He drew him out of his hidden place, and made his poison a medicine, so that the poison for destroying the body became a medicine for healing the spirit. For what hurts the body benefits the spirit (1 Cor 5:5).

41.0.22.en: So let me allow the serpent to strike what is earthly in (my body); let me allow it to bite my flesh and cause it to turn livid, and the Lord will say of me: "Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life" (Job 2:6).

41.0.23.en: What a power of God! He entrusts the keeping of man's soul to the hand of Satan, who wants his destruction...! By the Master's commandments He made Satan the keeper of His sheep, so that against his will he came to carry out the commandments of heaven, and by his harshness to obey the commandments of meekness!

41.0.24.en: * Such great distress and heavy grief came upon the demons and their soldiers on the day of the crucifixion of our God, because at His death and descent into Hades He did to them what He did to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, and freed the children of Adam from their prison as He freed the children of Israel from the land of Egypt.

41.0.25.en: St. Ambrose * Despite (the devil's) much boasting in speech and his insolence, the Savior seized him with a hook like a great dragon (Job 41:1), and like a beast the bridle was put in his jaws, and like a fugitive He bound his nostril with a rope, and pierced his lips with a thorn (Job 41:2); the Lord bound him like a bird that we might mock him (Job 41:5), and with him the demons his companions, like serpents and scorpions (Lk 10:19), that we might crush them and tread them under our feet.

41.1.0.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic Canst thou put a rope into his snout? or bore his jaw through with a hook? [2]

41.1.1.en: "Canst thou put a rope into his snout": the Septuagint reads: [Wilt thou put a ring in his nostrils?]. Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that his two nostrils refer to his deceitfulness, while the ring refers to the omnipotence of the divine power.

41.1.2.en: If the enemy of good does not cease to breathe out his deceptions and wiles as with his nose, so that man may fall into a chain of sins, and despair comes upon him and he does not rise, the mighty mercies of God nullify these deceptions, and man is filled with hope of forgiveness of his sins, and rises by the grace of God working in him.

41.1.3.en: Some hold that he is speaking here about the ornaments with which the Egyptians adorned the crocodile as a god. But it is clear that the talk here is not about deifying the crocodile and adorning it, but about its violence and the impossibility of taming it.

41.1.4.en: Rope (agmon): the exact translation means a kind of cord. It is as if he meant here that Leviathan has a marvelous strength, so that it is impossible to put a cord around his ear to bind his jaws. It was the custom in the East to put a ring in the ear of bulls and buffaloes and lead them by it.

41.1.5.en: Hook (choach): it is in truth a ring. It was, and still is, the custom to put a strong iron ring in the jaw of a large fish when it is caught, and the fisherman ties a cord to the ring and leaves the fish in the water, to draw it out when he finds someone to buy it.

41.2.0.en: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft words unto thee? [3]

41.2.1.en: When a man falls into captivity he is crushed and humbles himself, but not so the enemy of good, who does not surrender or humble himself with many entreaties, for he does not submit quickly. He is like a beast of prey which, even after being caught, does not calm down but hopes to devour the one who caught it. The enemy of good is fierce and does not know the language of tenderness.

41.2.2.en: * If these words are addressed to the person of the Son, then (Satan) speaks soft words addressed to the Incarnate One, saying: "I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God" (Lk 4:34). This leviathan makes many supplications to Him when it was said to Him by Legion: "If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine" (Mt 8:31).

41.2.4.en: * Satan is always diligent, even when danger comes upon him of losing his prey.

41.2.5.en: * Why does he return to attack? What do we learn from this? For even if we fall a thousand times, Satan will not stop, but continues the war without any hesitation.

41.2.6.en: * Observe that he goes about the world at every moment. Zechariah teaches us that the angels walk to and fro through the earth (Zech 1:10-11). But this wretch is not content with going about, for divine providence also does this work; he goes about in order to be condemned the more (for his evils), and that we may be the more on our guard. For this reason he was called [the ruler of the darkness of this world] (Eph 6:12); that is, the prince of evil.

41.2.7.en: Speak, O Satan, what have you done? He says: I have gone to and fro in the earth, I have walked up and down in it, and here I am.

41.2.8.en: What did he bring? He brought nothing useful or good, and so he did not answer why he went about.

41.2.9.en: St. John Chrysostom If the enemy of good does not know submission, he will not rest from resisting, even if he is overcome once and many times. But the Lord Christ cast out demons from many, and in humiliation the demons sometimes confessed Him as the Holy One of God, lest He torment them, and sometimes asked that He permit them to enter into the swine, as they said: Why art thou come to torment us? So he who bears the Lord Christ within him, the demons are confounded before him, as if they were entreating him to cease fighting them by his prayers and his deep communion with the Savior.

41.2.10.en: When we make a renewed practical covenant with God, the enemy of good collapses, for the believers are freed from the covenant which they had previously made with him. And, marvelously, instead of their being slaves of the devil, he becomes a slave to them, so that even if he breathes out his poisons, his wiles and his deception against them, all this is turned into their edification, their approval and their glorification.

41.2.11.en: * Through the sufferings the Lord ascended on high and led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men (Ps 68:18; Eph 4:8), and gave to those who believe in Him authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy, that is, authority over the leader of the apostasy.

41.2.12.en: St. Irenaeus * Here protective care goes hand in hand with permission to strike, and the divine plan is fulfilled through protection and through the forsaking of the chosen servant, for while He forsakes him He guards him... So the saint was delivered into the hand of the adversary (Job 2:6), but his soul was kept in the hand of (God) his helper, for he was among the flock of whom the Truth says in the Gospel: "Neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand" (Jn 10:28).

41.2.13.en: Moreover, they do not see Lucifer rising, he of whom Isaiah said: [Lucifer, which shone in the morning], and then goes on: [cut down to the ground] (Isa 14:12), indicating that he does not regain his former honor. By his fall from heaven to earth he wanted the destruction of man, but God gives the one who is not deceived authority to tread the traitor under his feet and shatter him to pieces.

41.3.0.en: Abba Hesychius of Jerusalem Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever? [4]

41.3.1.en: It refers to the animal mentioned: even if it falls into the snare it will not enter into a covenant with man, nor accept to serve him as a slave; it cannot be tamed.

41.3.2.en: We often think that we are strong, that sin will not harm us and the enemy cannot deceive us, so we are lax with sin and open the door to the enemy of good, thinking that he is enslaved and can serve us.

41.3.3.en: Eve opened the door to Leviathan, and entered into a dialogue with the serpent, and wished to establish a covenant, she and her husband and her offspring, with the devil and his hosts. She thought that the enemy would serve her, as he showed her the way to enjoy divinity and knowledge, and she fell into the humiliation of slavery to him. Dialogue with the enemy of good and entering into covenants with him will not avail, but leads us down to eternal destruction.

41.3.4.en: The devil made many offers to the Lord Christ during the temptation on the mountain, and when He rejected all his offers, "the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him" (Mt 4:11).

41.3.5.en: * You are not the only one who does evil, but there is one who pushes you to it violently. He is Satan, who suggests evil to you without having compulsory mastery over the one who accepts it. Therefore the Preacher says: "If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place."

41.3.6.en: Close your door and drive him far from you, so that he does no harm to you; but if you accept the thought of lust without care, its roots will penetrate you, and your mind will be seduced by his wiles, and he will plunge you into the abyss of evils.

41.3.7.en: You may say: I am a believer; lust cannot come up upon me even if I think about it much!

41.3.8.en: Do you not know that the trunk of a tree, by continual resistance, can break even a rock?! So do not allow the seed to be found in you, lest it tear your faith apart and shatter it. Uproot evil by its root before it blossoms, lest through your negligence at the beginning you need axes and fire afterwards.

41.3.9.en: Treat your eyes in due time when they become inflamed, lest you become blind and need a physician!

41.4.0.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens? [5]

41.4.1.en: A tamed bird can be played with for amusement and entertainment, but it is not so with Leviathan. For amusement birds are caught and put in cages so that young girls may stand around them enjoying the sight of them. In some undeveloped countries fathers tie birds with a string so that their children may play with them as a kind of amusement.

41.4.2.en: The enemy of good thinks of himself that he is the prince of this world, that no one has authority over him, and he did not realize that when the incarnate Word offered Himself as a sacrifice for the whole world, he lost his kingdom and became like a captive with no power or strength, whom little children courageously drag to trample him under their feet.

41.4.3.en: God raises up from the believers the army of spiritual salvation, which has no enemy but the devil and his angels. He trains His believers in spiritual combat, and gives even little children the possibility of victory, so that it is said of the Church, which was like dry bones cast in the midst of a valley: "The breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army" (Ezek 37:10); as it is also said of her: "Awesome as Jerusalem, as an army with banners" (Song 6:4).

41.4.4.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that Satan, in his deception, uses every means to deceive man: he appears as the one who eats grass like the ox, as if he were a four-footed animal; again he appears as Leviathan in the waters, caught with a hook; and finally he appears as a bird in the air. He pursues man wherever he is, whether on land, or in the sea, or flying in the air. He is in the stupidity of animals despite his dangerous, deadly and attractive wiles, but in stupidity he lost his glory and his eternity; and he is wicked like the dragon in the sea, who does not cease to harm by every means, and he is proud, his heart is lifted up and he exalts himself like one who flies on high.

41.4.5.en: * Surely the Lord played with him as with a bird when He showed him the bait in the sufferings of the only-begotten Son of God, but He caught him in the net.

41.4.7.en: * We find in Job this creature being played with by the heavenly angels, and the Lord gave His disciples authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy.

41.4.8.en: Theodoret of Cyrus * We look in amazement at His boundless and unutterable love, His infinite longsuffering, and His forgiveness at every moment of our sins which we confess to Him without measure, and His calling us despite our former unworthiness, but by His grace and mercy. Also the opportunities of salvation which He offers us without limit, giving us adoption, caring for us from childhood with grace and the knowledge of His laws. And He granted us to overcome by Him the enemy (Satan) through His good will in us, offering us eternal happiness and unfading crowns. Likewise His undertaking the economy of the Incarnation for our salvation and the breadth of the wonders of His mysteries which He offers to all the Gentiles.

41.4.9.en: Abba Moses * In ordinary battles the commanders do not arm women or children or old men, but our Commander, the Lord Christ, distributes this royal weapon (which is the possession of Christ Himself) to all equally. Then He teaches them the military stratagems of the devil.

41.4.10.en: Abba Theodoret * Follow the heavenly Bridegroom, that you may stand firm against the invisible enemies.

41.4.11.en: Wage war against principalities and powers (Eph 6:12), and first draw them away from yourself, so that they have no portion in you, and afterward drive them away from those who flee to you seeking protection through your counsel.

41.4.12.en: Cast them down under your feet as their leader and defender.

41.4.13.en: Do you renounce those disputations that are against the faith in Christ?

41.4.14.en: Fight with the word of godliness against the wicked, evil counsel. As the Apostle says: "Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God" (2 Cor 10:5). Put your trust above all in the arm of the great King, at the mere sight of whom His enemies fear and tremble.

41.5.0.en: St. Basil the Great Shall the company of fishers dig a pit for him? or shall they part him among the Canaanites? [6]

41.5.1.en: Since Leviathan was a source of terror and represented a great danger, the fishermen did not care to catch him by any means, for the troubles of catching him do not equal their gains if they divide him among the merchants.

41.5.2.en: By the company here is meant the company of fishermen who join together to catch him in a net or a certain snare.

41.5.3.en: "Or shall they part him among the Canaanites?" The Septuagint reads: "Do the Gentiles feed on him?" and the Vulgate: "Do friends cut him up?"

41.5.4.en: The Canaanites were known as merchants; will they then divide him into parts, to sell him?

41.6.0.en: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears? [7]

41.6.1.en: Large fish are usually caught with spears, but it is hard to catch the crocodile with spears, because it cannot be wounded by a spear unless it strikes him in the belly, which is hard to reach. For his back is covered with very strong scales which the spear cannot pierce.

41.6.2.en: Here he alludes to an instrument representing a spear in the shape of a fish with two tongues, often found engraved on Egyptian monuments. This spear was a slender rod ten to twelve feet long, with double feathers at the end like the modern arrow. It had two sharp ends about two feet long, encircled by a fish. The fisherman pushes it in the Nile, in a flat boat among the papyrus reeds and lotus plants, when he sees his prey with fins, and he draws the instrument with his right hand and moves it in the form of a bow with his left hand.

41.7.1.en: The blessed Job, however great his righteousness, must remember the battle that took place between him (in the person of his parents Adam and Eve and their offspring) and Satan, for because of its bitterness man does not try to enter again into a battle with this crocodile. He says to him: Touch him if you dare. Good, but remember the previous battle before you begin trying to undertake a new battle, otherwise the results will be dire.

41.7.2.en: * The holy Job prophesied of the coming of the Lord, of whom he truly said that He would defeat the great leviathan (Job 41:8), and it has happened! For He struck the terrible leviathan, Satan, and cast him down, and humbled him in the last times by the honored sufferings of His body.

41.7.3.en: St. Ambrose God warns the blessed Job against entering into a battle with the devil by his own strength, thinking that he is able to lay his hand upon him, that is, to dominate him and overcome him.

41.7.4.en: * What if the Almighty God lightened the burdens we bear, but withdrew His help from us and left us amid the trials of this leviathan? Where shall we go when a strong enemy rises up against us, if we find no shelter in any protection of our Creator?

41.7.5.en: If you see the sword of the adversary attacking you, do not tremble at the blows of a father to you. For you see the blows with which I strike you, but you do not perceive the danger of the enemy from whom I free you by means of my blows to you... Therefore keep silence more and more while you are under the discipline of a father, and you will see the more that you are weak in regard to the attacks of the enemy. When you are struck by my correction of you, that you may acquire patience while you bear it, remember your enemy and do not count what you suffer as hard, for through the outward sufferings you are freed from the inward sufferings.

41.7.7.en: Behold, the hope of him is in vain.

41.8.0.en: Shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? [9]

41.8.1.en: There is no hope of overcoming him, for it is a vain hope. As soon as man looks upon this enemy he falls. The mere looking at him takes away man's hope and courage. This is what happens when one looks at the crocodile.

41.8.2.en: * Victory is not achieved by the amount of money, nor by pride in strength, nor by loftiness of glory, but the Lord gives His help freely to those who seek it with intense sorrows. So it was with Paul, who made his sorrows the object of his boasting. Therefore he was able to say: "When I am weak, then am I strong"...

41.8.3.en: Do you see where sorrows lead you? To the hope that maketh not ashamed (Rom 5:3).

41.8.4.en: St. Basil the Great * Let us not allow despair to possess us, for we have many incentives in good hope. Even if we sin every day, let us draw near to Him, entreating and supplicating, asking forgiveness of our sins, for in this way we draw further from sin, the nearer the time to come, and so we drive away Satan, and call upon the love and compassion of God, and receive the blessings of the age to come by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and His love for mankind.

41.9.0.en: St. John Chrysostom None is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me? [10]

41.9.1.en: There is no wise man who would provoke the crocodile, or enter into a battle with him; how then can anyone stand before God Himself as an adversary and resist His plan, His judgments and His wisdom? If this is the position with a creature that God brought into being to be under the feet of man, to whom God gave authority over creation, how can man take a stand of rebellion against his Creator? Who can stand before God in His wrath?

41.9.2.en: *By the strong man is meant Satan, and his house is nothing but his kingdom on earth, while his goods are those people who imitate the devil their father in their affairs and works. Just as we call the saints holy vessels and consecrated goods, so the wicked may be called the goods and vessels of the devil, for they share with him in wickedness and evil. Christ the Word alone entered the house of the devil, this earthly world, and bound Satan in [chains of darkness and cast him down] (2 Pet 2:4). Levi was saved and was no longer a captive in the kingdom of Satan, and by his repentance became worthy of divine blessings, so we learn that repentance is the right way to salvation and redemption, for it was said: "Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth" (Isa 45:22).

41.9.3.en: *It is enough for you what Habakkuk pointed out as he denounced the enemies of the Apostles: "Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his, and to him that ladeth himself with pledges! Shall they not rise up suddenly that bite thee, and awake that vex thee, and thou shalt be for booties unto them?" (Hab 2:6-7). For Satan has gathered into his fold all the inhabitants of the earth, who are not his, and made them bow down to him and worship him, and so he became burdened and magnified; but some awoke to despoil him of his spoils, for the Apostles cast the net of their teaching upon the captives and sinners, and returned with it to God filled with the people of the whole world.

41.9.4.en: St. Cyril the Great * [He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the false accuser] (Ps 72:4). Rightly is Satan called "the false accuser," for he slandered God, and because of envy claimed that God had forbidden eating from the tree (of the knowledge of good and evil), and he slandered Job with lies, saying: "Doth Job fear God for nought?... Put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face" (Job 1:9, 11). In the eighth psalm he gave him the two names "the enemy and the avenger," while here (Ps 72:4) he calls him a false accuser.

41.10.0.en: 11 "Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine. 12 I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion. 13 Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle? 14 Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about. 15 His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal. 16 One is so near to another, that no air can come between them. 17 They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered. 18 By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. 19 Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out. 20 Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron. 21 His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth. 22 In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. 23 The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved. 24 His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone. 25 When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves. 26 The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon. 27 He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood. 28 The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble. 29 Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear. 30 Sharp stones are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire. 31 He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment. 32 He maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary. 33 Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear. 34 He beholdeth all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride."

41.10.1.en: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him?

41.10.2.en: Whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine [11].

41.10.3.en: Some hold that the expression here means: "Who does a kindness, that I may return it to him?"

41.10.4.en: Others hold that he means: who can foretell what will happen? If man cannot foretell what will happen when he is hunting a predatory beast, how then does he think he is able to subdue the Creator Himself, or to repay Him for His kindnesses? Who thinks that he is able to give me anything, when I am the owner of everything? It is fitting for man to submit to the Creator, and to accept everything with thanksgiving.

41.11.0.en: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion [12].

41.11.1.en: Here He begins to give a detailed description of Leviathan, about whom He had already spoken in this chapter in general terms. He says: I cannot keep silent about speaking of his mouth and his teeth and his scales and the eyelids of his eyes and the openings of his nose, and his neck, and his heart.

41.11.2.en: The animal referred to here is not described to bring out its beauty, but as one who has great power and is exceedingly fierce: "his power, and his comely proportion (grace) of his armor," or the beauty of his weapons. The subject of His discourse is not the beauty of the animal, but its weapons of defense.

41.12.0.en: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can come to him with his double bridle? [13]

41.12.1.en: No one can discover the face of his garment or his covering, that is, take off his hard, deceitful garment, to see his inner skin, nor can anyone dare to put a bridle on his jaws, as is done with other animals when they are bridled. It is not possible for anyone to dare to bring a double bridle to restrain the two rows of his teeth.

41.12.2.en: * This leviathan tempts the minds of the religious in one way, and the minds of those who are devoted to this world in another. For he openly presents to the wicked the evils they desire, but he secretly casts snares for the good, and deceives them under the appearance of holiness... Therefore the Apostle Paul, seeing some devoting themselves to the service of their bellies under the cloak of preaching, says: "For Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light. Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness" (2 Cor 11:14-15). Joshua feared this transformation when he saw an angel and asked him on which side he was, saying: "Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?" (Josh 5:13).

41.12.4.en: Who can open the doors of his face?

41.13.0.en: His teeth are terrible round about [14].

41.13.1.en: He calls his mouth "the doors of his face," for it is like a gate with two leaves.

41.13.2.en: This applies more to the crocodile, for Bochait says that the teeth of the crocodile number thirty, which is a large number, and their sizes are large compared with the size of its body; some of them protrude outside, and some are serrated like a saw, so that when it seizes its prey it cannot escape from it.

41.13.3.en: The Septuagint reads: "Who shall open the doors of his face?"

41.13.4.en: * [The doors of his face] are the wicked teachers, who are called the gates of his face, for everyone enters through them so that this leviathan is seen as if he were in his royal power... For when their vain preaching is accepted, the door of destruction opens for the wretched hearers.

41.14.0.en: His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal [15].

41.14.1.en: Rows of his scales cover him like shields; his body includes 17 rows, and there is no possibility of piercing his body except through his eyes or his throat (when he opens his mouth), or his belly.

41.14.2.en: Umbreit and Prof. Lee hold that the word "his pride" here in the original Hebrew is geewoh, which is like gewah or gevah, meaning a back, since the crocodile's back is covered with scales.

41.14.3.en: When the crocodile closes its mouth it becomes as if sealed with wax, so that no air leaks out from between its jaws and between its teeth.

41.14.4.en: *Satan is hard and without pity, and in his depths he never rests, for Holy Scripture says of him: [His heart is hard as a stone, and he stands like the hard anvil of a smith] (Job 41:24) LXX. But the saints have trampled him under their feet by the power of Christ, for He said: "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you" (Lk 10:19). Therefore Christ says: "Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not."

41.15.0.en: St. Cyril the Great One is so near to another, that no air can come between them [16].

41.16.0.en: They are joined one to another, they stick together (are congealed), that they cannot be sundered [17].

41.16.1.en: * The scales of sinners are hard and bound together, so that it seems that no breath of life can pierce the mouth of the preachers. For those who practice similar sins gather together, in an evil defense, and become together in an obstinate agreement, so that each protects the other with a common defense of their sins. For each is afraid for himself when he sees another being rebuked or corrected... And while they protect one another in fellowship in their evils by their wicked motive, they do not allow the breath of holy counsel to reach them by any means... Union strengthens perversion, and makes them even more incorrigible, and so they become united together in unanimity.

41.17.0.en: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning [18].

41.17.1.en: Amphibious animals dive into the water and hold their breath for a long time and then suddenly breathe out forcefully, so that it is as if they were sneezing, while they turn their eyes toward the sun so that they seem as if radiating fire, or they expel their breath so that it appears as if it were sunbeams.

41.17.2.en: [The eyelids (lids) of the morning]: the Egyptians depict the eyes of the crocodile as protruding forward as if they signified the early morning. When the crocodile rises to the surface, the first thing that appears of it is its eyes, before its whole body, so that it is like the appearance of the morning.

41.17.3.en: Some hold that since the crocodile remains under the water a long time, it rises to the surface to expel the water with a strong rush from the two openings of its nose, so that it appears like a rainbow.

41.17.4.en: When the crocodile is in the water its eyes appear dim or dull, but when it rises toward the surface they appear very bright.

41.17.5.en: * Anthony said: The demons often appear in this manner, as the Lord revealed to Job, saying: [His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. Out of his mouth go burning lamps, and sparks of fire leap out. Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron. His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth] (Job 41:18-21). So the chief of the demons appears, as I said before, terrifying, and speaking with boasting and arrogance, as the Lord condemned him when He said to Job: "He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood" (Job 41:27). [He esteemeth the sea as a bath of water, and the bottom of the abyss as his captive, and the deep as a path for him] (Job 41:31-32). And as He said through a prophet: [The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake] (Ex 15:9). And He said through another prophet: [I will seize the whole world in my hand like a nest, and I will lift it up as one lifts abandoned eggs] (Isa 10:14). These things the demons boast of, and promise them to those who fear God in order to deceive them. Therefore it is fitting for us who are believers not to fear the appearances (of the devil) nor to heed his words, for he is a liar and never speaks the truth.

41.17.6.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic Out of his mouth go burning lamps.

41.18.1.en: The animal is described here as one who vomits fire, for when it opens its mouth and its fangs appear, it emits fire upon those around it. Or like one who breathes and sends out violent fiery breaths that kill the prey and burn it.

41.18.2.en: * The lamps proceed from his mouth, for (the wicked teachers) kindle the minds of their hearers with the love of erroneous opinions, and while they seem to shine with wisdom, they burn with evil.

41.19.0.en: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as out of a seething pot or caldron [20].

41.19.1.en: This simile applies to the horse used in battles, which sends out from its nostrils the smoke of burning fire.

41.19.2.en: * The dense breath of leviathan comes out of the two openings of his nose, for the evil of his pride issues forcefully from the puffs of his manifest wickedness... The smoke is said to come out of the two openings of the nose, by the deception of his miracles, which for a moment begets doubt even in the hearts of the elect. Smoke goes out of the mouth of leviathan because of false wonders, so that there is a threatening mist that corrupts the eyes even of those of good minds.
